question: During violent anti-government protests in Tirana yesterday, Albanian police officers burst into the courtyard of the Resurrection of Christ Orthodox Cathedral, pursuing and brutally arresting protesters who had sought refuge there.

The Orthodox Autocephalous Church of Albania condemned the raid, stressing that the sanctity of the space was violated and emphasising that places of worship must not become battlegrounds1. The Union of University Employees of Albania also issued a statement, expressing its concern about police violence against student protests2.

Bearing in mind that respect for religious sites and places of worship has been a pillar of the rule of law and Western culture since ancient Greece and given that Albania is a candidate country, can the Commission answer the following questions: 1.
Is it aware of the police violence which took place in the courtyard of the Resurrection of Christ Orthodox Cathedral in Tirana?
How does it view the attitude of the Albanian authorities, including with regard to Albania’s status as a candidate country?
What actions will it take towards the Albanian Government to ensure that such incidents are never repeated?
